title: Electric Potential and Capacitors
summary: The potential at a point is the work done per unit positive charge in bringing it from infinity: V = W/q. It is a scalar, measured in volts (1 V = 1 J/C).
The potential of a point charge is V = q/4πε₀r. It falls as 1/r, decreasing non-linearly as you move away from a positive charge. Potential difference V_A − V_B = W_AB/q.
Potential energy of a charge in a field: U = qV. For example, −1 µC at 100 V has U = −10⁻⁴ J.
The relation between field and potential is E = −dV/dr, so in a region of constant potential the field is zero.
Every point on an equipotential surface has the same potential. No work is done in moving a charge along it, and E is perpendicular to it.

Two equipotential surfaces can never intersect, because the meeting point would have two potentials and two field directions. For a point charge they are concentric spheres; for a uniform field, parallel planes.
A conductor's surface is an equipotential, so no work is done in moving a charge between two points on a charged sphere.
For two spheres at the same potential, kq₁/r₁ = kq₂/r₂, so q ∝ r.
C = Q/V, measured in farads (1 F = 1 C/V; µF and pF are common). Capacitance depends on the size and shape of the conductors, their separation and the medium, but not on the charge or the voltage.
Parallel-plate capacitor: C = ε₀A/d in air and Kε₀A/d with a dielectric of constant K, so a dielectric multiplies C by K. A thin metal foil placed midway between the plates leaves C unchanged.
Series: 1/C = 1/C₁ + 1/C₂ + … Parallel: C = C₁ + C₂ + … Ten 5 µF capacitors give 50 µF in parallel and 0.5 µF in series, a ratio of 100 : 1.
U = ½CV² = Q²/2C = ½QV, stored in the electric field between the plates.
Battery disconnected (Q constant): increasing d makes C fall and V = Q/C rise; inserting a dielectric makes C = KC₀, V = V₀/K and U = U₀/K.
Battery connected (V constant): doubling d halves C and halves U; inserting a dielectric makes C and U grow K times, while E = V/d stays unchanged.
On a Q–V graph the slope is C, so at the same V the steeper line (larger C) stores more energy.

vsa: What is an equipotential surface? Why can two equipotential surfaces not intersect?

A surface on which every point has the same potential; no work is done moving a charge along it.
If two intersected, the common point would have two different potentials and two field directions, which is impossible.
A capacitor is kept connected to a battery of voltage V. How does the energy stored change when the plate separation is doubled?
C = ε₀A/d halves when d is doubled. With V fixed, U = ½CV² also halves.
The Q–V graphs of two capacitors X and Y are straight lines, X being steeper. Which stores more energy at the same voltage?
The slope Q/V = C, so X has the larger capacitance. U = ½CV², so at the same V, X stores more energy.
Write the expression for the energy stored in a capacitor in three forms.
U = ½CV² = Q²/2C = ½QV. It is stored in the electric field between the plates.
sa: A 2 µF air capacitor is charged to 12 V and the source removed. A slab of dielectric constant 5 then fills the space. Find the ratio of the energies stored before and after.

Before: U₁ = ½CV² = ½ × 2 × 10⁻⁶ × 144 = 1.44 × 10⁻⁴ J.
Q stays constant; C becomes 5 × 2 = 10 µF.
After: U₂ = Q²/2C' = U₁/5 = 2.88 × 10⁻⁵ J.
U₁ : U₂ = 5 : 1 (energy is drawn into the slab).
Derive the expression for the energy stored in a parallel-plate capacitor of capacitance C charged to potential V.

While charging, at charge q the p.d. is q/C. Adding dq needs work dW = (q/C) dq.
Total work W = ∫₀^Q (q/C) dq = Q²/2C.
With Q = CV: U = ½CV² = ½QV, stored in the field between the plates.

la: Derive the capacitance of a parallel-plate capacitor and show how a dielectric changes it. How do the charge, p.d., field and energy change when a dielectric slab is inserted (a) with the battery connected and (b) after disconnecting the battery?

Plates of area A, separation d, charge ±Q: σ = Q/A, E = σ/ε₀, V = Ed = Qd/ε₀A, so C = Q/V = ε₀A/d. With a dielectric filling the gap, E is reduced K times, so C = Kε₀A/d.
(a) Battery connected (V fixed): C → KC; Q → KQ; E = V/d unchanged; U = ½CV² → KU.
(b) Battery disconnected (Q fixed): C → KC; V → V/K; E → E/K; U = Q²/2C → U/K.
Define electric potential and potential difference. Derive the potential at a point due to a point charge, and state the relation between field and potential.

Potential at a point: the work done per unit positive charge in bringing a test charge from infinity to the point, V = W/q₀ (volt = J/C). Potential difference between A and B is W_AB/q₀.
Point charge q: the field at distance x is kq/x². The work against it from ∞ to r is W = −∫∞^r (kq/x²) q₀ dx = kqq₀/r, so V = q/4πε₀r.
Relation: E = −dV/dr — the field points in the direction of decreasing potential, and E = 0 where V is constant.
